title: Feasibility study of vertigo diagnostics using a smartphone – VertiGo V
summary:
Smartphone-based eye movement analysis is a promising new approach for assessing dizziness. It uses the phone’s camera and specialized software to record and analyze eye and head movements. Compared with conventional systems, this method may offer advantages such as lower cost, greater mobility, and easier access, especially in rural or underserved areas.

Recent studies suggest that smartphone-based solutions can be feasible and reliable in clinical use. At the same time, there are still technical and regulatory challenges, for example regarding camera position, lighting conditions, and software performance. Overall, this technology is still in an early but rapidly developing stage.

interventions.name: Patients with acute vertigo are examined with the vertigo app.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age ≥ 18 years
Acute or chronic vertigo symptoms
Capacity to give consent
Sufficient knowledge of German
Exclusion criteria:
Incapable of giving consent
Pregnancy
Minor age
Refusal of consent or withdrawal of consent
Language barrier without an interpreter
Neurodegenerative diseases, acute inflammatory diseases of the central nervous system, pronounced visual or eyelid movement disorders
Patients in acute emergency situations
